config.title: Simple Todo List — CRUD with TypeScript

intro.title: Simple Todo List — CRUD with TypeScript
intro.body: You will build a small todo app: add tasks, mark them complete, and delete them. You will use React `useState` for list state, TypeScript interfaces for your data shape, and controlled patterns for list updates (map, filter, immutable updates). By the end you will have a clear CRUD loop you can reuse in dashboards, carts, and admin UIs.
intro.usecase: The same pattern appears everywhere: task lists, shopping carts, notification queues, and editable tables. Managing an array in state, deriving UI with `map`, and updating with pure-style setters is core React work.

objectives: Establish a Todo interface with id, text, and completed fields and declare useState<Todo[]> so the contract is explicit, and data shape and updates remain explicit throughout the lesson.
Implement an addTodo function that uses the array spread operator to append a new typed object to state so the feature works end to end and the resulting behavior can be observed and explained.

Implement a toggleTodo function that uses .map() to return a new array with one item's completed field flipped so the feature works end to end and the resulting behavior can be observed and explained.

Implement a deleteTodo function that uses .filter() to return a new array excluding the item matching a given id so the feature works end to end and the resulting behavior can be observed and explained.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the `useState` hook from the `react` package.
steps.hint: Use: `import React, { useState } from 'react'` (or `import { useState } from 'react'` if your setup allows).
steps.expectedOutcome: Imports are present so the file can use JSX and `useState`.
successCriteria: The file is ready for a component and hooks.
steps.feedbackCorrect: ✅ Imports look good. Next: define the `Todo` type.
steps.feedbackWrong: You need `import` lines for React and `useState` from `'react'`.

steps.title: Define Todo interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript `interface Todo` with: `id` (number), `text` (string), and `completed` (boolean).
steps.hint: Use `interface Todo { id: number; text: string; completed: boolean }` — numeric ids pair naturally with `Date.now()` or an incrementing counter.
steps.analogousExample: interface Item { id: number; label: string; done: boolean }
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Define Todo interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: A `Todo` interface describes each task for the rest of the lesson.
successCriteria: `Todo` includes `id` as `number`, plus `text` and `completed` with correct types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: ✅ `Todo` is defined. Next: scaffold the list component.
steps.feedbackPartial: Include all three properties with `id: number`, `text: string`, and `completed: boolean`.
steps.feedbackWrong: Declare `interface Todo` with `id: number`, `text: string`, and `completed: boolean`.

steps.title: Create main TodoList component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named `TodoList` that returns a JSX `<div>` wrapper (you will fill it in later).
steps.hint:
Use `const TodoList = () => { ... return (
...
); };` or `export default function TodoList()`.
steps.expectedOutcome: A `TodoList` component exists as the root of the UI.
successCriteria: Component is named `TodoList` and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackPartial: Ensure the component is named `TodoList` and returns a `<div>`.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add a function component `TodoList` that returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize todos state
steps.instruction: Inside `TodoList`, initiate a state var called `todos` typed as `Todo[]` and initial value set to an empty array or initial demo items if you prefer.
steps.hint: Typing the state as `Todo[]` helps TypeScript catch mistakes in handlers.
steps.expectedOutcome: List state is ready to hold todo objects.
steps.feedbackCorrect: ✅ State is initialized. Next: add the labeled new-todo input in the JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: Declare state with `useState` and a `Todo[]` type.

steps.title: New todo field (label + input)
steps.instruction: In the `return`, add a `<label>` whose text is `new todo` and a `<input type="text" />` for typing the next task. Link them with `htmlFor` on the label and a matching `id` on the input (for example `new-todo-input`). Do not add `value` or `onChange` yet—you will connect this field to React state in the following steps.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form control exists in the UI before it is made controlled.
steps.feedbackCorrect: ✅ The field is on the page. Next: store the draft text in state.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use paired `htmlFor` and `id`, and `type="text"` on the input.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add a label reading `new todo` and a text input, associated with `htmlFor` and `id`.

steps.title: State for new todo text
steps.instruction: Declare a state variable to hold the text the user will type into the new todo field, and bind that state to the `<input>` from Step 5 using `value={newTodoText}`. You will add `onChange` in a later step so keystrokes update this state.
steps.hint: String state for form drafts almost always starts as an empty string: `useState('')`.
steps.expectedOutcome: Draft text lives in state and is bound to the input’s `value` before `onChange` is wired.
steps.feedbackCorrect: ✅ State is bound to the field’s `value`. Next: add a change handler for that draft.
steps.feedbackPartial: Add `useState('')` for the draft and pass `value={newTodoText}` to the text input.
steps.feedbackWrong: Declare `newTodoText` with `useState` and set `value={newTodoText}` on the new-todo `<input>`.

steps.title: Handler for new-todo text changes
steps.instruction: In `TodoList`, add an `onChange` handler named `handleNewTodoChange`. Each time it runs, take the current text from the event (`e.target.value`) and pass it to `setNewTodoText`. Type the event parameter as `React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>`. Define it after your state hooks and before the `return`—you will pass it to the `<input>` in Step 8; for now, only implement this function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A named handler updates the draft string from a change event; the input already uses `value={newTodoText}`.
successCriteria: A function like `handleNewTodoChange` is defined inside `TodoList`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: ✅ Change handler is defined. Next: render the controlled input that uses it.
steps.feedbackPartial: Declare `handleNewTodoChange` with the typed event and call `setNewTodoText` with `e.target.value`.

steps.title: Make the new-todo input controlled
steps.instruction: On the `<input>` that already has `value={newTodoText}`, add `onChange={handleNewTodoChange}` and a helpful `placeholder`. Keep the same `id` and `<label htmlFor>` pairing from Step 5. Reference the handler by name—do not duplicate the change logic inline in JSX.
steps.hint: Controlled field: `value` from state (Step 6), `onChange` points at your handler function.
steps.expectedOutcome: Keystrokes update `newTodoText` because both `value` and `onChange` are set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: ✅ Controlled input is wired. Next: implement `addTodo`.
steps.feedbackPartial: Add `onChange={handleNewTodoChange}` and a `placeholder` to the input that already has `value`.

steps.title: Create addTodo handler
steps.instruction: Add `addTodo(text: string)` that appends a new `Todo` with a unique numeric `id`, the given `text`, and `completed: false`. Use `setTodos` with a new array. You already have `newTodoText`, `handleNewTodoChange`, and the controlled input from the previous steps; a later step will wire the button to call `addTodo(newTodoText)`.
steps.hint: `setTodos((prev) => [...prev, { id: Date.now(), text, completed: false }])` keeps updates immutable and satisfies `id: number`.
steps.analogousExample: setTodos((prev) => [...prev, { id: Date.now(), text, completed: false }]);
steps.expectedOutcome: New tasks can be added without mutating the previous array.
successCriteria: `addTodo` takes a string and calls `setTodos` with a new todo.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use `setTodos` and spread or functional update to append; new items need a numeric `id` (e.g. `Date.now()`).
steps.feedbackWrong: Implement `addTodo` with `setTodos` and a new `Todo` object whose `id` is a number.

steps.title: Create toggleTodo handler
steps.instruction: Add `toggleTodo(id: number)` that flips `completed` for the todo with that `id` (map over todos and return updated objects).
steps.expectedOutcome: Clicking a checkbox can toggle completion in state.
successCriteria: `toggleTodo` uses `setTodos` and `map` to update one item.
steps.feedbackPartial: Map todos and flip `completed` when `id` matches; the parameter should be typed as `number` to match `Todo.id`.

steps.title: Create deleteTodo handler
steps.instruction: Add `deleteTodo(id: number)` that removes the todo with that `id` using `filter`.
steps.expectedOutcome: A todo can be removed from state by id.
steps.feedbackPartial: Filter out the matching numeric `id` and set state.

steps.title: Add Todo button and clear input
steps.instruction: Add a button labeled `Add Todo` with `type="button"`. On click, call `addTodo(newTodoText)` and then `setNewTodoText('')` to reset the field. Optionally ignore empty strings.
steps.hint: `onClick={() => { addTodo(newTodoText); setNewTodoText(''); }}` or guard if `!newTodoText.trim()` return.
steps.expectedOutcome: Users can submit the draft text to add a todo and see the field clear.
successCriteria: Input clears after add (or is ready to).
steps.feedbackPartial: Include `<input>`, placeholder text, and a button `Add Todo`.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add a text input and button in the returned JSX.

steps.title: Render todos list
steps.instruction: Map `todos` to a list: show text, a checkbox (`checked={todo.completed}`), and a Delete button. Use `key={todo.id}`.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each todo row shows text, checkbox, and delete control.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use `map`, `key`, checkbox, and a delete button per row.
steps.feedbackWrong: Map `todos` to JSX with stable keys and controls.

steps.title: Wire handlers to todo items
steps.instruction: Wire `onChange` on the checkbox to `toggleTodo(todo.id)` and `onClick` on Delete to `deleteTodo(todo.id)`. Ensure the Add button uses `addTodo(newTodoText)` and clears the field. Export `TodoList` as default.
steps.hint: `onChange={() => toggleTodo(todo.id)}` and `onClick={() => deleteTodo(todo.id)}` — for controlled checkboxes use `checked` + `onChange`.
steps.expectedOutcome: Full CRUD loop works in the editor preview: add, toggle, delete.
successCriteria: Checkbox and delete call the correct handlers with `todo.id`.
Add flow calls `addTodo` with the input text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: ✅ Todo CRUD with TypeScript is wired end to end.
steps.feedbackPartial: Connect `onChange`/`onClick` to `toggleTodo`/`deleteTodo` and add from input.
steps.feedbackWrong: Ensure handlers receive `todo.id` and the Add button uses `addTodo`.
